title: The Roman emperor found hiding behind a curtain
hook: A Roman guard found the next emperor hiding behind a curtain.
summary: After Caligula was murdered in AD 41, his lame, mocked uncle Claudius hid in terror, was found by a guard, and was made emperor of Rome.
sources: Suetonius, Life of Claudius 10: a soldier saw Claudius's feet under a curtain, dragged him out and hailed him emperor.
Josephus, Antiquities 19; Encyclopaedia Britannica 'Claudius': Caligula killed 24 January AD 41, Claudius became emperor, ruled to AD 54, invaded Britain AD 43.

lines.text: A Roman guard found the next emperor hiding behind a curtain.
lines.caps: A Roman *guard | found the next *emperor | behind a *curtain

lines.text: In forty-one A.D., Caligula had just been murdered.
His lame uncle Claudius was sure he was next.
lines.caps: His *lame uncle Claudius | was sure he was *next

lines.text: So he hid, but a soldier saw his feet under the curtain.
lines.caps: So he *hid, | but a soldier saw his *feet | under the *curtain

lines.text: The guards dragged him out, then bowed and hailed him emperor.
lines.caps: They *dragged him out, | then *bowed | and hailed him *emperor

lines.text: Everyone had always laughed at him, so nobody had thought him a threat.
lines.caps: Everyone *laughed at him, | nobody saw a *threat

lines.text: He ruled thirteen years and conquered Britain.

post.caption:
The weakest man in Rome became its emperor because everyone had underestimated him.
Would you have hidden too?
